headline: Learned models predict, generate, and personalize gut microbiome compositions
label: Learned Microbiome Models
summary: Three preprints from May 2026 extend learned sequence representations to microbiome prediction, synthetic generation, and personalized diet design.
synthesis: The shared thread is learned models operating directly on microbiome data, applied to three tasks: prediction, generation, and intervention design. Susagi applies a permutation-invariant denoising transformer to sets of bacterial SSU rRNA embeddings, learning a member-level stability function that supports zero-shot microbiome prediction. The Second Brain uses a diffusion generative model with a sparsity-preserving decoder to produce synthetic human microbiome profiles, evaluated on American Gut Project data. MPDR learns diet-microbe interactions from paired cohort data and optimizes personalized diets toward desired gut microbial compositions. What is new relative to single-sequence embedding classifiers is the treatment of microbial communities as sets, the enforcement of sparsity in generative outputs, and the inversion of learned models into diet recommendations. All three items are preprints, so the results remain unreviewed.
